formula: dbh.cm ~ SSasympOrig(age.bh, asymptote, scale), asymptotic regression through the origin; tree-specific asymptote and scale (fixed and random = asymptote + scale ~ 1 | tree.ID); correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 2)
notes: NONLINEAR: read gutten.Rd (von Guttenberg 1915 Norway spruce stem analyses; Robinson and Hamann 2010) and the book code the package ships, inst/resources/scripts/book/fitting_models.r: gutten.d <- groupedData(dbh.cm ~ age.bh | tree.ID), gutten.nlme.0 <- nlme(nlsList(dbh.cm ~ SSasympOrig(age.bh, asymptote, scale))) with fixed and random asymptote + scale ~ 1, then gutten.nlme.1 <- update(gutten.nlme.0, correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 2)), whose intervals the chapter reports; gutten.nlme.2 tries SSasymp with three parameters, and a try() lets scale depend on site. The book drops rows without dbh.cm. tree is the tree number within location, which tree.ID combines; height, volume and age.base are alternate responses and an alternate age; site and location are tree-level columns no model keeps. Hand check #162: stands; 107 trees of 5-15 rows. The book's other fits (gutten.nlme.0 without the ARMA residuals, the three-parameter SSasymp, the site-dependent scale in a try() and an unevaluated GAMM) share its response and grouping and file no row.

formula: log(vol.m3) ~ log(dbh.cm) + (1 | plot)
notes: Read sweetgum.Rd (Lenhart's sweetgum trees from Texas, one row per felled tree, plot the plot it was felled in, vol.m3 integrated from a spline over the stem measures; Robinson and Hamann 2010 section 2.4.2) and the book code the package ships (inst/resources/scripts/book/regression.r): sweetgum.lm.ld <- lm(log.vol.m3 ~ log.dbh.cm), trees treated as independent, so the plot design is rendered as a random intercept. tree is the tree id; dbh.in and height.ft are the imperial copies of dbh.cm and height.m; stump.ht.ft and height.m are usable columns. Hand check #162: stands; 15 plots of 1-5 trees.

formula: log(height.m) ~ dbh.cm * species + (1 | plot)
notes: Read ufc.Rd (Upper Flat Creek forest cruise 1991, trees measured on variable radius plots; Robinson and Hamann 2010) and the book code the package ships (inst/resources/scripts/book/regression.r): hd.lm.1 <- lm(I(log(height.m)) ~ dbh.cm * species, subset = height.m > 0) and the weighted hd.lm.5 <- lm(height.m ~ dbh.cm * species, weights = dbh.cm^-2), trees treated as independent; ufc.r sums the trees to their sample point. The trees-within-plots design is rendered as a plot random intercept. tree is the tree label within plot. Hand check #162: stands; 132 plots of 1-8 trees.

formula: vFA ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro, 08-Introduction-to-Multilevel-Models.Rmd at b04814b5), open-ended exercise 3 Project 5183: game logs of 7 Rockies starting pitchers (ID) who started games before and after the 75-pitch limit of June 20, 2012 (PCL); key responses vFA, K.9 (the column K/9), ERA and Pitpct, PCL the primary covariate, Coors and Age confounders to control. The book fits no model but warns of variance components at 0 and correlations at 1, so the pitcher-level PCL slope is proposed. Responses in page order: rows 2 and 3 are K/9 and ERA, the fourth, Pitpct, is ignored. The other game statistics are game outcomes or the parts of the responses (SO, ER, IP, Str, Pit), ignored; Opp (opponent) and Team are no documented factor. Hand check #162: stands; 7 pitchers of 7-24 starts, PCL varying within each. Pitpct, the fourth key response, is past the three models.

formula: `K/9` ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 exercise Project 5183, the second key response (strikeouts per nine innings, K.9 in the book); design and proposed model as row 1. Hand check #162: stands; K/9 is the column's name in the file.

formula: ERA ~ PCL + Coors + Age + (PCL | ID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 exercise Project 5183, the third key response (earned runs per nine innings); design and proposed model as row 1. Hand check #162: stands.

formula: cbind(made, shots - made) ~ ball + order + distance + (1 | id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: the file is in the book repository at b04814b5; ch. 6 (ch-logreg) open-ended exercise 4, Trashball, has a class toss paper ten times from each of three distances for a binomial model, but it names no file and fits no mixed model. Each id shoots twice, once with a tennis and once with a ping-pong ball (ball) in a counterbalanced order (order), making made of shots throws from a distance set per shooting group; id is the grouping a reader would model, rendered as a random intercept. group (shooting group, nests the ids) and the shooter traits (year, basketball, height, hand, glasses, HSsports, awake, underhand, sleep) are left as unused columns. Hand check #162: the Trashball exercise corrects the reading's note that no chapter describes the file; 20 shooters of 2 rows, 6 or 9 shots per row.

formula: price ~ overall_satisfaction + reviews + room_type + accommodates + bedrooms + minstay + district + WalkScore + TransitScore + BikeScore + PctBlack + (1 | neighborhood)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro) open-ended exercise 2, Airbnb in Chicago (Trinh and Ameri 2018): 1561 listings merged with information on their neighborhood (1 of 43), asked to build a multilevel model for price with listing- and neighborhood-level traits; no model is fitted, the formula is proposed from the listed variables. district (1 of 9, Chicago's districts, a neighborhood-level classification) is a covariate. HighBlack is derived from PctBlack and not a column. Row 2 is the ch. 11 exercise on the same table. Hand check #162: stands; 43 neighborhoods of 1-330 listings.

formula: I(overall_satisfaction == 5) ~ price + reviews + room_type + accommodates + bedrooms + minstay + district + WalkScore + TransitScore + BikeScore + PctBlack + (1 | neighborhood)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 1, Airbnb in Chicago: satisfaction = 1 if overall_satisfaction is 5, else 0, modeled by a multilevel generalized model with listing and neighborhood traits; no model is fitted, the formula is proposed. The documented response is the binary recode of overall_satisfaction, a half-star rating, so response_type records what the column holds (ordinal) while the formula keeps the source's binary recode. Hand check #162: the recode stays in the formula by its ruling.

formula: ambiguity ~ incumbent + democrat + mismatch + abs(ideology) + distLean + attHeterogeneity + demHeterogeneity + (1 | distID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 8 (ch-multilevelintro) open-ended exercise 1, Political ambiguity: Chapp et al. (2019, Social Science Computer Review, Going Vague) fit a multilevel model for candidates' ambiguity scores with predictors at the candidate and the district level (distID), per the book; the paper was not read, so the formula is built from the hypotheses the book quotes (incumbency 1b, ideological distance mismatch 2a, ideological extremity as abs(ideology) 2b, attitudinal and demographic heterogeneity 3a and 3b) and the listed controls democrat and distLean. name is the candidate's label. Row 2 is the ch. 4 count response of the same table. Hand check #162: no, since the exercise asks the reader to fit their own models and Chapp et al.'s paper (Social Science Computer Review 37(5), 2019, doi:10.1177/0894439318791168) is paywalled, so its formula is unverified and the row is a proposal. 435 districts of 2 candidates.

formula: totalIssuePages ~ ideology + democrat + (1 | distID)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 4 (ch-poissonreg) guided exercise 7, Going vague: totalIssuePages, the number of issues a candidate comments on, modeled by a hurdle model with ideology and democrat in both parts (pscl hurdle, Poisson count part); the book fits no random effect, and the district intercept comes from the two-level structure ch. 8 documents for the same table. The formula names the count part; both parts take the same covariates. Hand check #162: stands; part (d) fits ideology and democrat in both the zero hurdle (binary) and the zero-truncated Poisson count part, part (e) adds ideology:democrat to both, and the formula states (d)'s count part.

formula: removed ~ pvi2 + cperhs + cmedin + cperba + days2000 + obama + freqchal + sexexp + antifamily + occult + language + homosexuality + violence + (1 | state) + (1 | book)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 3, Book banning (Fast et al. 2011): challenges in U.S. states 2000-2010 without Texas, removed the primary response, predictors at the state level (pvi2, cperhs, cmedin, cperba), the book level (freqchal) and the challenge level; the page notes that a book can be challenged in several states and for several reasons, so state and book are crossed grouping factors. The page asks for multilevel models and fits none; the formula is proposed from the listed variables. booktitle labels book; author (books nest in authors) is no documented factor. Hand check #162: state stays a grouping factor by the exhaustive-units ruling, against the outside check's design factor: 47 states (Texas removed), removed varying within 38, and the exercise names state-level predictors. 694 books, 120 challenged more than once.

formula: rate ~ I(year - 2002) + instpct + instamt + faculty + tuition + faculty:I(year - 2002) + tuition:I(year - 2002) + (I(year - 2002) | id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) open-ended exercise 2, Completion rates at U.S. colleges (IPEDS 2002-2009): rate the response, Level 1 predictors year, instpct and instamt, Level 2 predictors faculty and tuition, asked for multilevel models of baseline (2002) rates and their change to 2009; no model is fitted, so the growth model with the Level 2 predictors on intercept and slope is proposed in the book's two-level convention. instname labels id; state (institutions within states) is no documented factor. Hand check #162: stands; random_slopes names the column year and the formula its centered term I(year - 2002), against the outside check's expression in random_slopes. 1,310 institutions of 1-8 years.

formula: I(Vote == "1") ~ zfaminc + zmedinc + EconWorse + EducStatus + republican + EducStatus:republican + EconWorse:zfaminc + EconWorse:republican + (1 | inputstate)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 6 (ch-logreg) guided exercise 5, 2016 Election (CCES, Renier et al. 2018): model1a glm(Vote01 ~ zfaminc + zmedinc + EconWorse + EducStatus + republican + EducStatus:republican + EconWorse:zfaminc + EconWorse:republican, family = binomial), Vote01 = 1 for a Trump vote (Vote holds 1 or Other). The page plots one observation per state, carries state-level covariates (zmedinc, propforeign) and asks in part (h) whether the independence assumption holds, so voters are grouped by inputstate, rendered as a random intercept. Theory 2's immigration model (Noimmigrants) shares response and grouping and is not a row. faminc and medinc are the raw forms of zfaminc and zmedinc; inputstate_post repeats the state. Hand check #162: inputstate stays a grouping factor by the exhaustive-units ruling, against the outside check's flat reading: 50 states of 64-3,680 voters.

formula: mathn ~ female * sch_ses * dis_size + (female | dis_id:sch_id) + (1 | dis_id)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) guided exercise 2, Kentucky math scores (Bickel 2007): eighth graders in middle schools in districts, three levels. Model B adds female, nonwhite and their interaction at Level One; Model C drops the interaction and adds sch_ses to all Level Two equations; Model D drops nonwhite and adds dis_size to all Level Three equations, rerun with an error term only on the Level Three intercept, the version the exercise carries on with (3-way female, sch_ses, dis_size interaction); written here, the school-level female slope following the book's convention of an error term per Level Two equation. The exercise states the model level by level and asks the reader to fit it; it gives no lmer call. A school code recurs across districts, so the school factor is dis_id:sch_id. readn is an alternate response, stud_nm the student id. Hand check #162: yes, since the exercise states reduced Model D (dis_size in every Level Three equation, an error term on the Level Three intercept alone). Models A to C and the unreduced D share its response and grouping and file no row. 132 districts, 236 schools.

formula: Area ~ Species + Zone + Strata + Tree.height + Tree.girth + Branch.length + (1 | Tree) + (1 | Branchnum)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) open-ended exercise 2, Mudamalai leaf growth (Pray 2009): 5 trees from each of 3 species in each of 3 climate zones (the page numbers trees 1-5 within zone, but the file numbers them 1-45), 3 branches from each of 3 strata per tree, 5 leaves per branch; leaf Area the response of interest, asked for a multilevel model and no model fitted, so the formula is proposed. Branchnum identifies a branch (Branch is its number within tree and stratum). Area was computed from Length and Width by regression for most leaves, so both are ignored. Herbivory, petiole sizes and Stomata (per stratum per tree) are left as unused columns. Hand check #162: Tree replaces Species:Zone:Tree, the same 45 groups of 27-46 leaves; each of the 405 branches (Branchnum) lies in one tree.

formula: SYS ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 (ch-lon) open-ended exercise 1, UCLA nurse blood pressure study (Goldstein et al. 2000, data from Weiss 2005): 40-60 readings per nurse (SNUM) over one day, systolic BP the primary response, asked for multilevel models relating work conditions (activity, mood, work status) to BP trends; no model fitted, the formula is proposed from the listed variables. Responses in page order: rows 2 and 3 are DIA and HRT, the alternatives the page names; it also suggests modeling the mood ratings, which here are covariates. timept indexes the reading; time (minutes from midnight) is left as an unused column. Hand check #162: stands; 203 nurses of 28-60 readings. The mood ratings STR, HAP and TIR, which the page suggests modeling too, are past the three models.

formula: DIA ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 1, diastolic BP, the first alternative response the page names; design and proposed model as row 1. Hand check #162: stands.

formula: HRT ~ MNACT5 + STR + HAP + TIR + DAY + POSTURE + PHASE + AGE + FH123 + timepass + (1 | SNUM)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 1, heart rate, the second alternative response the page names; design and proposed model as row 1. Hand check #162: stands.

formula: HEIGHT ~ I(YEAR - 1990) + I(YEAR - 1990):TUBEX + (I(YEAR - 1990) || ID) + (I(YEAR - 1990) || TRANSECT)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 10 (ch-3level) guided exercise 1, Tree tubes (Eisinger et al. 2011): the long table, one row per tree and year, a three-level model for height with years within trees (ID) within transects; Model C is the unconditional growth model in TIME = YEAR - 1990 with uncorrelated random effects at levels two and three, and Model D adds the TUBEX by TIME interaction alone (part j). Ch. 7 (ch-corrdata) fits lmer(growth_yr1 ~ tubes + (1|transect)) on first-year growth, the 1991 minus 1990 height of each tree, a pivot of two rows that no column holds, so it is no row. SPECIES is left as an unused column. Hand check #162: the formula takes Model D without TUBEX's main effect, against the reading. covariates keep TUBEX, since an interaction's parts are covariates, and random_slopes names the column YEAR, the registry's form, against the outside check's YEAR alone and its expressions; so the contract adds TUBEX's main effect. Models A to C share its response and grouping and file no row. 9 transects of 526 trees, TUBEX constant within each transect.

formula: stars_given ~ length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 (ch-GLMM) open-ended exercise 4, Yelp restaurant reviews in Madison (Mohr 2018): reviews of restaurants by reviewers, the page noting that user and restaurant can be crossed random effects; its first modeling idea is the number of stars (or whether it is 5), the others whether at least one person found the review useful (row 2) or cool (row 3). No model fitted, the covariates are proposed. The table has no restaurant id, so name is the restaurant factor (a chain's branches share it). avg_user_stars and avg_biz_stars average the response, text is free text, year_index repeats year, funny is an unused vote count. Hand check #162: stands; the 888 names hold about 1,018 restaurants by name, average stars and review count, 20,635 users. The five-star recode is past the three models.

formula: I(useful > 0) ~ stars_given + length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 open-ended exercise 4, the second idea: whether at least one person thought the review useful, with user and restaurant crossed; design and proposal as row 1. The documented response is the binary recode of the vote count useful, so response_type records what the column holds (count) while the formula keeps the source's recode. Hand check #162: the recode stays in the formula by its ruling.

formula: I(cool > 0) ~ stars_given + length + year + rev_count_user + rev_count_biz + (1 | user_id) + (1 | name)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 11 open-ended exercise 4, the third idea: whether at least one person thought the review cool; design and proposal as row 1. The response is the binary recode of the vote count cool, as row 2. Hand check #162: the recode stays in the formula by its ruling.

formula: I(QN66 == 1) ~ I(Q2 == "Female") + bmipct + I(c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)[as.integer(Q81)]) + (1 | stratum:psu)
notes: BeyondMLR ch. 6 (ch-logreg), case study Reducing the risk of obesity: the 2009 Youth Risk Behavior Survey; the chapter's code reads this file, draws 500 students (set.seed(33)), recodes Q66 to lose.wt (trying to lose weight), Q2 to sex, Q84 to sport and Q81 to media hours, keeps complete cases and writes risk2009.csv, on which it fits glm(lose.wt.01 ~ female + bmipct + media, family = binomial) (model4; sport was dropped). QN66, the survey's own trying-to-lose-weight indicator, is that recode. The book treats students as independent; the survey's primary sampling unit psu (within stratum) is a cluster the rows repeat within, rendered as a random intercept, at low since no source fits it. weight is the survey weight; the book enters Q81 as numeric hours. Hand check #162: the formula takes the book's recodes: QN66 is 1 exactly where Q66 is Lose weight (7,378 rows) and 2 elsewhere, female is Q2 == "Female", and Q81's seven levels are the hours 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 (the book's code shifts as.numeric(Q81)). 55 PSUs of 87-617 students.
